fresh_facts.fact: KIUC has restored power to more than 80% of members (81% as of Sunday/reported Monday 12:04am); roughly 8,000+ members still out, concentrated on the North Shore between Moloaa and Haena with scattered pockets Anahola-Kekaha-Kokee
KIUC CEO David Bissell's full quote (existing sheet truncated it): 'We will know much more in the next couple of days as we gauge the progress of our crews.'

A THIRD Hurricane Lowell-related death confirmed: a 59-year-old man found dead near Kuhio Highway/Wainiha Powerhouse Road in Wainiha, Kauai, in an area with significant Lowell-related flooding; police confirmed it as the 3rd Lowell-linked death

Statewide Hurricane Lowell death toll is now 3: Steven Palama, 74, found near Nomilu Fishpond on Kauai's south shore (storm-surge related, found ~Sept 8-9); the Wainiha man, 59 (flood-related, found Sept 11, confirmed Sept 12); and one man in Waimanalo, Oahu, killed when a tree fell on his tent (~Sept 7-8)
Hawaii's congressional delegation letter urging Trump to approve Major Disaster Declarations for both Lowell and Lala — as of this letter, declarations remained pending/not yet approved

Most Kauai DOE public schools reopened Monday, Sept 14; Kilauea Elementary and Hanalei Elementary remained closed to students due to lack of utilities — Kilauea reopens to students/staff Tuesday Sept 15, Hanalei reopens to staff Tuesday and students Wednesday Sept 16; 12 of 15 school campuses had power back as of the prior Friday

Kaumalapau Harbor on Lanai resumed LIMITED operations (a Young Brothers interisland fuel barge landed after underwater hazards were cleared); landside repairs will continue for several more weeks before full reopening; next fuel shipment expected the following Wednesday

Hawaiian Electric (Oahu) had already restored the vast majority of its Lowell-related outages by Sept 9 (down to ~440 customers, mostly Makaha Valley) and shifted crews to help KIUC on Kauai — this is now stable background, not a live figure

No official FEMA/state dollar damage total for Lowell has been published; only a private catastrophe-modeling estimate exists (Cotality: $0.5-1.0 billion in insured losses, mostly Kauai) and Gov. Green has said the damage cost will be in the hundreds of millions, with formal assessments still ongoing

tracking_line: Officials have NOT yet said: whether President Trump has approved the Major Disaster Declaration request for Lowell (still pending as of the Sept 14 congressional letter); a hard date for 100% KIUC power restoration (KIUC's Bissell says only "in the next couple of days" as of Sept 14); an official FEMA/state dollar damage total for Lowell specifically (only a private Cotality estimate of $0.5-1.0B in insured losses exists); a final injury count beyond "at least one"; a confirmed date for Kaumalapau Harbor's full landside reopening (still "several more weeks" as of Sept 14) or for Port Allen's return to full commercial operations; and whether any further storm-related deaths remain under investigation beyond the three confirmed.
